result.summary: Sets `SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE` instead of `SO_REUSEADDR` on P2P listen sockets on Windows, preventing other local sockets from binding to the same port. Also adds a functional test checking that another process cannot bind to an active P2P listen port.
result.problem: On Windows, `SO_REUSEADDR` does not guarantee exclusive ownership of a port; a second process running under the same user account can also bind to the port using `SO_REUSEADDR` and intercept incoming P2P connections intended for bitcoind.
evidence: Commit c6971fd610: 'On Windows, `SO_REUSEADDR` does not give sockets exclusive use of an address and port, so another process running under the same user account can bind to the same port and intercept incoming P2P connections.'
Description cites Microsoft Winsock documentation explaining that `SO_REUSEADDR` permits port hijacking by processes with matching security contexts unless `SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE` is set.
result.card: Sets SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE instead of SO_REUSEADDR on P2P listen sockets on Windows, accompanied by a test verifying port exclusivity. On Windows, default SO_REUSEADDR semantics permit another process under the same user account to bind to an in-use port and intercept incoming P2P connections. This extends socket exclusivity protections added for RPC listeners in merged PR #36169.

risk.why: A failure in setting socket options or unexpected socket binding errors on Windows could prevent bitcoind from binding its P2P listener on startup or restart.
